playoff_odds.how: 10,000 simulated seasons: each remaining game's score is drawn from that team's own weekly scores (with under 4 weeks, every team's scores shifted to its mean), and teams are seeded by wins, then total points, as the league's settings say.

record_vs_median.how: Each week my score against the median of every team's score that week, beside all-play (my score against every other team's each week).

lineup_efficiency.how: Each week the best lineup my roster allowed under the league's slot rules, with hindsight, minus what I started; ranked against every team (1 = fewest points left on the bench); and, apart, waiver adds that out-produced their baseline but sat on my bench.

start_sit.how: A close call is a starter and the best-projected bench player who could fill that slot projected within 3 points of each other; it was right if the starter scored at least as much.

consistency.how: Standard deviation of my weekly scores divided by their mean (lower = steadier), ranked against every team (1 = steadiest).

strength_of_schedule.how: The season scoring average of each opponent I've played, averaged, minus the league's average weekly score; ranked against every team (1 = hardest schedule).

draft_value.how: For each of my picks, its rank in points per game among every drafted player who has played, minus where it was drafted (negative = better than its draft slot).

waiver_impact.how: Points scored in my starting lineup by players I didn't draft (waivers, free agents, trades), and their share of my starters' points.

position_share.how: Share of my starters' points from each position, beside the average of every team's shares.

schedule_what_if.how: My scores replayed against each other team's opponents week by week (where that opponent was me, against that team instead); how many of those schedules give me a better or worse record.

margins.how: My score minus my opponent's each completed week; close games are decided by under 5 points.

waiver_adds.how: Each add after the draft, judged on his points while on my roster against the dropped player's points per game elsewhere, else the replacement level. Out-producing it is a hit (captured or benched), else a miss, stash or insurance. The value is the hit rate with a 95% Wilson interval.

acquisition_split.how: Points scored in each team's starting lineup over the completed weeks, split by how the player reached that roster (drafted; a waiver claim or free-agent pickup; a trade; otherwise kept or commissioner-moved), mine against the league's median team on each split.

draft.how: Each of my picks' points to date while on my roster (started or benched over the completed weeks, nothing after a drop) against the median of the same for every player taken in that round league-wide; value is my residuals summed.

quadrant.how: For every team in my leagues over the completed weeks: the all-play win share (my score against every other team's each week, ties half) against luck, actual wins minus the sum of weekly all-play shares. My teams carry a week-by-week trail; other teams are labelled points.

draft.how: Points per week my picks scored on my roster above their round's baseline: each league's pick points standardised, the round's mean across my leagues mapped back onto each league's scale. The interval is a bootstrap over my picks; rank and percentile are among every manager across my leagues.

lineup.how: Points per week my set lineup gave up against the best legal lineup by the projections known at each player's kickoff, from the last snapshot before it. A t-interval over my team-weeks, needing two weeks of snapshots; rank and percentile are among every manager across my leagues.

moves.how: Points per week from my waiver claims, pickups and trades: each acquired player's points on my roster from the move's week, minus what the players he replaced scored over the same weeks elsewhere, else their season average. Rank and percentile are among every manager across my leagues.

strength.how: My all-play win share over the completed weeks, pooled across my teams, with a Wilson interval; rank in each league and, for the percentile, among every manager across my leagues.

composite.how: The mean of the ok components' percentiles, the share of managers across my leagues I beat on each; the interval a bootstrap over the completed weeks, every component recomputed on each resample.

album_half_life.how: For albums with at least 10 plays in their first 7 days, an exponential decay fitted (Poisson, by maximum likelihood) to daily plays over their first 4 weeks; the median half-life across albums, and this week's most-played album with its half-life so far.

values.first_unit: one album with 10 plays in its first week, 4 weeks on and still decaying

discovery.how: Share of each month's plays by artists first played that month (none earlier in the archive); months with at least 50 plays, from the archive's second month.

values.first_unit: one month after the archive's first with 50 plays

album_listener.how: Share of plays whose previous play, within 15 minutes, is the preceding track of the same album.
album_listener.missing: track number on the album (scrobbles carry the album's name only)

concentration.how: Each month (with at least 50 plays) the five most-played artists' share of plays, the same by ISO week while the archive is young (every week with a play, with its play count); and the most plays of one track in one day; the value is the latest week's share.

heatmap.how: Plays by weekday (Monday first) and hour, Pacific; and plays per weekday against per weekend day, over every day since the first play.

genre_mix.how: Each month's plays (months with at least 50) by the artist's top Last.fm tag, the 8 largest named, the rest as other; artists not yet looked up are untagged.

comebacks.how: Artists with at least 20 plays in a month after 3 or more months with none (and some play before that), newest first.

first_repeat.how: Hours between a new track's first and second play (new = first played after the archive's first 30 days); the median over tracks played twice.

values.first_unit: one track first played after the archive's first 30 days and played a second time

entropy.how: Shannon entropy, in bits, of plays across artists, by month (months with at least 50 plays) and by ISO week while the archive is young (every week with a play), with the equivalent number of equally played artists, 2 to the entropy; the value is the latest week's.

nostalgia.how: The median release year of the tracks played each month (months with at least 50 plays and 25 with a known year) and by ISO week; the value is the latest week's. Release years come from Last.fm's album wiki, else the Apple Music library; plays with neither are left out.

retention_new_artists.how: For each month after the archive's first, the share of artists first played that month with another play within 30 and 90 days. A month is listed once every first play's 30 days are up, the 90-day figure null until those are; the value is the latest 30-day share.

values.first_unit: one month after the archive's first whose new artists are all 30 days past their first play

enduring.how: From Apple Music's lifetime play counts: each artist's plays divided by the years since their first track entered the library. Most tracks entered on the day the library was synced, not at a first listen, so the rate is plays per year of library membership; the top 15.

artist_survival.how: Months an artist stays in rotation, from their first track entering the library to their last play; a play in the last 60 days counts as ongoing. Kaplan–Meier curves by discovery type, a log-rank test and Cox hazard ratios. Cohort: artists added after the export's first recorded play.

values.ph_check: Schoenfeld residuals against event order: r = -0.06, p = 0.72, no sign the new-against-catalog hazard ratio changes over time
values.cohort: Artists first added on or after 2024-08-15, the export's earliest recorded play; 283 added earlier are left out.

artist_survival_all.how: Months an artist stays in rotation, from their first track entering the library to their last play; a play in the last 60 days counts as ongoing. Kaplan–Meier curves by discovery type, a log-rank test and Cox hazard ratios. Every artist counted, sync-day additions dated from the sync.

values.ph_check: Schoenfeld residuals against event order: r = -0.07, p = 0.39, no sign the new-against-catalog hazard ratio changes over time
values.cohort: Every artist with a play, the 167 in the library at the 2023-06-30 sync counted from that day.

album_listening.how: For each album in the Apple Music library with at least 5 tracks and 20 plays, the Gini coefficient of plays across its tracks (0: every track played equally; near 1: one track has them all). The value is the share of such albums below 0.4, played as albums.

tier_completion_pace.how: For each tier, completion (finished over finished plus dropped; this falls below 1 only if a tiered title is later dropped) and, for shows and anime with at least 3 dated titles in the tier, the median pace in episodes a week; backfilled watches never count.

s_tier.how: The share of tiered titles in S, by type and by release decade (decades with at least 10 titles), and for each genre on at least 10 titles its share among S titles over its share among B titles with a bootstrap interval. Tiers cover finished titles only.

tier_model.how: An ordered logistic model of my tier on type, the eight most common genres, release decade, runtime and Simkl's community score, numeric features standardised. Scored by leave-one-out accuracy against guessing the commonest tier; each effect in log-odds with a bootstrap interval. Tiers cover finished titles only.

taste_drift.how: Mean tier score of the titles I finished in each year, from the dated finish (a film's watch, a show's last logged episode), years with at least 10 dated finishes. The value is a straight line's slope per year; undated (backfilled) titles are left out. Tiers cover finished titles only.

community_gap_by_genre.how: For each genre on at least 10 titles, my tier score standardised over every tiered title minus Simkl's community score standardised the same way, the mean with a 95% t-interval (positive where I rate the genre higher than the community does). Tiers cover finished titles only.

pace_vs_tier.how: Mean tier score (S 5 to D 1) of finished shows and anime with dated episode logs, by the weeks from the first to the last logged episode: under 2 weeks, 2 to 8 weeks, over 8 weeks; backfilled watches are left out. Tiers cover finished titles only.

by_director.how: For each director (TMDB credits) with at least 3 of my tiered films, the mean tier score with the films and their tiers, best first; a pair credited on the same films is one row. The value is the top director's mean. Tiers cover finished titles only.

scores.how: Median and quartiles of my Beli scores, overall and by cuisine and by city (groups of at least 5 places).

choice_vs_taste.how: Each cuisine's share of the places I've tried against its share of my top quartile by score (cuisines with at least 5 places; the rest together as other).

order_effect.how: Score against the order places were ranked (1 = first), within cuisine (a fixed effect for each), as the change in score per 100 places with a 95% interval. Beli moves a place's ranked date when it's re-ranked.

contrast_effect.how: Score against the previous place's score (in the order ranked), within cuisine, as the slope with a 95% interval (positive: a good place before lifts the next one).

home_bias.how: Scores in my most-ranked city against everywhere else, within cuisine (a fixed effect for each), with a 95% interval; only cuisines tried both at home and away count.

contrarian.how: My scores against Beli's community score.
contrarian.missing: a community score (Beli's ranking response has none)

new_cuisines.how: Cuisines I ranked for the first time, counted by month (counts only, never which place); Beli moves a ranking's date when a place is re-ranked.

landing.how: For the 20 places I ranked most recently, in Beli's order, the percentile each sits at in my current ranking (1 = top): where a place just ranked sits is where it entered. The value is their median; there is no by-month table, since the archive keeps no ranked dates.
